correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed from the definition. CRT gives the exact local product. For \(m=\ell^a\), reduction modulo \(\ell\) gives one distinct root, while for \(p\ne\ell\) cyclicity of \(\mathbb F_p^\times\) gives either \(\varphi(m)\) primitive roots or none. After cancelling the \(\ell\)-factor, parity excludes every extra odd prime except one narrow \(\{2,q\}\) case when \(\ell\) is odd; that case reduces to \(m\mid\varphi(m)-1\), impossible. The converse is immediate. Direct computation for 3,990 pairs independently matched the definition, formula and equality locus. No finite computation is used to prove the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: Four targeted published-finding corpus searches returned no statement about Robu's \(\varphi_P\) specialized to prime-power cyclotomic polynomials or the equality locus \(\varphi_{\Phi_m}(n)=\varphi(n)\). The source paper was inspected in full HTML: it defines the function, develops the product framework and proves an asymptotic lower bound, but contains no occurrence of 'cyclotomic' and no coincidence theorem. Standard cyclotomic finite-field factorization gives only the local root count, not the global equality classification. Web searches for the exact combination of Robu's function, cyclotomic polynomials and equality with Euler's totient returned the Robu paper and generic cyclotomic references, not a covering theorem.
residual_risks: The generalized totient terminology is not unique across the literature; an older source using different notation for the same residue-counting function could have escaped keyword search.

No exhaustive bibliographic database search was available beyond published-finding corpus and web search, so originality remains a literature-search conclusion rather than a formal uniqueness certification.

value.rationale: The coincidence problem is intrinsic to a newly introduced polynomial analogue of Euler's totient: it asks when the new count actually reproduces the classical invariant. The theorem answers this exactly for the infinite and structurally central family of non-linear prime-power cyclotomic polynomials, not for an arbitrary finite slice. It also isolates the underlying prime of the cyclotomic index from the values of the generalized function, providing a reusable rigidity statement rather than a recomputed table.
